text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.
- Since 1990 the number of tourists visiting Norway has increased by 50 percent. This year 2.5 million visitors will spend around 15 billion crowns during their stay, research shows.

- Between 200 and 300 Albanians from the Serbian province of Kosovs who are living in Norway without residency permits could be sent back to their homeland. So far Norway has been prevented from sending the Albanians home because authorities there have refused to admit them.

- A day before the annual meeting of shareholders in insurer Storebrand, Orkla still refuses to say whether or not it will support the proposed merger with Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse. Food and beverage conglomerate Orkla holds 10 percent of the shares in Storebrand.
-Norway's trade surplus increased to 27.6 billion crowns during the first five months of 1997.

- U.S. oil company Marathon Oil Co claims the Norwegian state gives state-owned oil company Statoil illegal financial support. Marathon says the high tariffs paid by the state to send natural gas through Statoil's pipelines in the North Sea should be regarded as financial support.

- Environmental issues and Norway's work towards peace in the Middle East will be on the agenda of talks when Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto meets Norwegian premier Thorbjoern Jagland in the west coast city of Bergen on Thursday.
